text:
Lord, Lord, long ago, one day

I dreamed a love as no one ever could

dream it, some love that would be

all of life, all of poetry.


And winter passed and it did not come,

and spring also passed,

and summer persisted again,

and autumn found me with my waiting.


Lord, Lord; my back is bare,

make burst there, with rough hand,

the whip that bloodies the perverse!


For evening is already upon my life,

and this ardent and measureless passion

I have lost, Lord, making verses!




Languor, 1920

translation.title: The Plea
translation.editorial_note: The translation keeps the final bitter claim that poetry itself consumed the passion.
